324994.title: The normality–$K_5$-minor conjecture for cut polytopes
324994.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let ${\rm Cut}^\square(G)$ denote its cut polytope, and let $K[\operatorname{Cut}^\square(G)]$ denote the associated toric ring. A graph $H$ is a **minor** of $G$ if it can be obtained from $G$ by a sequence of edge deletions, edge contractions, and vertex deletions. The complete graph on five vertices is denoted by $K_5$.

**Normality–$K_5$-minor conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

$$
{\rm Cut}^\square(G)\text{ is normal};
$$

$$
K[\operatorname{Cut}^\square(G)]\text{ is Cohen--Macaulay};
$$

$$
G\text{ has no }K_5\text{-minor}.
$$

The conjecture extends the known implication that normality of ${\rm Cut}^\square(G)$ forces $G$ to have no $K_5$-minor. The converse, and hence the full equivalence, was stated as still open in the source.
324994.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2899

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2013). “Although the conjecture is still open, it is known that [] Let $H$ be a minor of a graph $G$.”

325405.title: Three-triangle matroid minor conjecture
325405.statement:
A **triangle** in a matroid is a circuit of size $3$. A matroid **admits** another matroid as a minor if that minor is obtained by deletions and contractions. **Three-triangle matroid minor conjecture.** If every element of a matroid $\mathcal{M}$ is contained in $3$ triangles, then $\mathcal{M}$ has one of

$$
\mathcal{M}(K_5),\qquad F_7,\qquad \mathcal{U}_{2,4}
$$

as a minor. The source gives no resolution; the conjecture is motivated by the Fano matroid, the uniform matroid $\mathcal{U}_{2,4}$, and the graphical matroid of $K_5$ as basic examples with this property.
325405.source_name: Boris Albar and Daniel Gonçalves, “On triangles in K_r-minor free graphs”, arXiv:1304.5468 (2013).
325405.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5468

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2013). “This conjecture has been proved for $k \leq 5$ but remains open for $k \geq 6$.”

325688.title: Vertex-contraction ideal conjecture for the Tutte polynomial
325688.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected undirected graph, let $s$ be a vertex of $G$, and let $N$ be the set of neighbors of $s$, excluding $s$. For each nonempty subset $W\subseteq N$, let $\overline{G_{/W\cup\{s\}}}$ denote the graph obtained by contracting $W\cup\{s\}$ in $G$ and removing all loops. **Vertex-contraction ideal conjecture.** The Tutte polynomial $T_G(x,y)$ belongs to the ideal generated by

$$
\left\{T_{\overline{G_{/W\cup\{s\}}}}(x,y):\emptyset\subsetneq W\subseteq N\right\}
$$

in $\mathbb{Q}[x,y]$. This conjecture would support the existence of a two-variable generalization of the Tutte polynomial for Eulerian, and possibly general, digraphs via recursive formulas involving vertex contraction.
325688.source_name: Kévin Perrot and Trung Van Pham, “Chip-firing game and partial Tutte polynomial for Eulerian digraphs”, arXiv:1306.0294 (2013).
325688.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0294

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2013).

325936.title: Forest embedding conjecture for tournaments
325936.statement:
Let $T$ be a tournament on $n$ vertices, and let $F$ be a **forest** on at most $n$ vertices with $c$ non-trivial components. **Forest embedding conjecture.** If $F$ has at most

$$
\frac{n}{2}+c-1
$$

edges, then $T$ contains every orientation of $F$.

The source states that this follows from Havet and Thomassé's theorem together with Sumner's conjecture, via a proposition. Since Sumner's conjecture is not presented as fully resolved, this derived conjecture is also not presented as resolved.
325936.source_name: Andrzej Czygrinow, Louis DeBiasio, H. A. Kierstead and Theodore Molla, “An extension of the Hajnal-Szemeredi theorem to directed graphs”, arXiv:1307.4803 (2013).
325936.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.4803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2013).

325990.title: The upper-bound comparison conjecture for Ramsey numbers with dropped cliques
325990.statement:
Let $r\geqslant 3$ be an integer, and let $k$ be an integer satisfying $3\leqslant k\leqslant r^{3/2}+r-1$. The quantity $g(r(k-2)+2,r)$ is the upper bound for the corresponding Ramsey number established earlier in the paper.

**Upper-bound comparison conjecture.**

$$
g(r(k-2)+2,r)<\binom{r(k-1)}{k-1,k-1,\ldots,k-1}=\frac{(rk-r)!}{((k-1)!)^r}.
$$

The conjecture compares the paper's bound $g$ with a multinomial upper bound in the stated range of $r$ and $k$. The supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
325990.source_name: Jonathan Chappelon, Luis Pedro Montejano and Jorge Luis Ramírez Alfonsín, “Ramsey for complete graphs with dropped cliques”, arXiv:1307.6327 (2014).
325990.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.6327

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2013).

326033.title: Maximal-length conjecture for inscribed kiss-free snakes
326033.statement:
Let $b$ and $k$ be positive integers, and consider kiss-free snakes inscribed in a rectangle of size $b\times k$. The length of an inscribed partially directed snake is $\left\lfloor \frac{(b+1)(k+1)}{2}\right\rfloor-1$. **Maximal-length conjecture.** The maximal length of a kiss-free snake inscribed in a $b\times k$ rectangle is

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{(b+1)(k+1)}{2}\right\rfloor-1.
$$

This conjecture has been generalized to tree polyominoes and proved by other authors, so the claim is solved.
326033.source_name: Alain Goupil, Marie-Eve Pellerin and Jérôme de Wouters d'Oplinter, “Partially Directed Snake Polyominoes”, arXiv:1307.8432 (2014).
326033.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.8432

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2013). “This fact which is the content of the following conjecture has recently been generalized to tree polyominoes and proved by a different group of authors (see ).”

326080.title: Reconstruction conjecture for quasi Cartesian products
326080.statement: A **quasi Cartesian product** is a graph with the local product-like structure described above. **Reconstruction conjecture.** Quasi Cartesian products can be reconstructed in essentially the same time from vertex-deleted subgraphs as Cartesian products. This predicts that the efficient reconstruction methods available for Cartesian products extend, up to essentially the same running time, to quasi Cartesian products; the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.
326080.source_name: Marc Hellmuth, Wilfried Imrich and Tomas Kupka, “Fast Recognition of Partial Star Products and Quasi Cartesian Products”, arXiv:1308.2101 (2013).
326080.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.2101

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2013).

326360.title: The minor conjecture for Cayley graphs of right groups
326360.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, let $R_k$ be a right zero band with $k$ elements, let $S=G\times R_k$, and let $C$ be a generating set. Write $\pi_G(C)$ for the projection of $C$ to $G$, and let $\underline{\operatorname{Cay}}(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote the underlying undirected Cayley graph. **Minor conjecture.** The graph

$$
\underline{\operatorname{Cay}}(G,\pi_G(C))
$$

is a minor of

$$
\underline{\operatorname{Cay}}(S,C).
$$

The conjecture was proposed as a stronger form of the preceding lemma, but it is false in general: the source explicitly notes that the analogous assertion for products $G\times S$ with $S$ not a right zero band fails.
326360.source_name: Kolja Knauer and Ulrich Knauer, “On planar right groups”, arXiv:1309.5236 (2014).
326360.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.5236

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2013). “Note that for products $G\times S$ of group $G$ and semigroup $S$ not being a right zero band the natural generalization of the conjecture is false.”

327190.title: Gracefulness of lobsters with almost perfect matchings
327190.statement:
Let $T$ be a lobster, and let an **almost perfect matching** mean a matching that leaves at most one vertex unmatched. **Gracefulness conjecture for lobsters with almost perfect matchings.** Every lobster with an almost perfect matching is graceful.

This is proposed as a special case of Bermond's conjecture. The source presents it as a statement for interested readers to prove, and does not give a resolution.
327190.source_name: Christian Barrientos and Elliot Krop, “Improved Bounds for Relaxed Graceful Trees”, arXiv:1402.0196 (2016).
327190.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.0196

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

327717.title: The dichotomy conjecture for directed graph homomorphism problems
327717.statement:
Let $H$ be a directed graph. The $H$-colouring problem asks whether an input directed graph admits a homomorphism to $H$.

**Dichotomy conjecture.** The $H$-colouring problem is polynomial-time solvable or NP-complete.

This conjecture seeks a complete complexity dichotomy for homomorphism problems to fixed directed graphs. The source states that it remains open; no graph-theoretic classification is known.
327717.source_name: Yangjing Long, “Graph Relations and Constrained Homomorphism Partial Orders”, arXiv:1404.5334 (2014).
327717.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.5334

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2014). “The conjecture is still open though many special cases of the conjecture have been verifies .”

329210.title: The full-support facet conjecture for ${\operatorname{LS}}_+$-perfect graphs
329210.statement: Let ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)$ denote the Lovász–Schrijver positive semidefinite relaxation of the stable set polytope. A graph is **${\operatorname{LS}}_+$-perfect** when ${\operatorname{LS}}_+(G)=\operatorname{STAB}(G)$, and a facet is **full-support** when its defining inequality involves every vertex of $G$. **The full-support facet conjecture.** If a graph is ${\operatorname{LS}}_+$-perfect and its stable set polytope has a full-support facet-defining inequality, then the graph is near-bipartite. This is presented as an equivalent formulation of the paper's open characterization problem for ${\operatorname{LS}}_+$-perfect graphs.
329210.source_name: S. Bianchi, M. Escalante, G. Nasini and L. Tunçel, “Lovász-Schrijver SDP-operator, near-perfect graphs and near-bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1411.2069 (2014).
329210.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.2069

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

330847.title: Shepherd–Sebő four-colour conjecture for t-perfect graphs
330847.statement: A graph is **$t$-perfect** if it satisfies the defining $t$-perfection property for graphs. **Shepherd–Sebő's four-colour conjecture.** Every $t$-perfect graph is $4$-colourable. This is a main open question about $t$-perfect graphs; four colours would be best possible, and the paper notes that $P_6$-free $t$-perfect graphs are $4$-colourable while the corresponding statement for $P_7$-free graphs is unknown.
330847.source_name: Henning Bruhn and Elke Fuchs, “t-perfection in P_5-free graphs”, arXiv:1507.00173 (2016).
330847.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.00173

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

330960.title: Ingleton's obstruction excluded-minor conjecture for base-orderability
330960.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a critical graph, let $P$ and $Q$ be the sets used to define the cyclic-flat lattice $\mathcal{Z}_\Delta^{P,Q}$, and let $M(\Delta)$ be the matroid with lattice of cyclic flats equal to $\mathcal{Z}_\Delta^{P,Q}$. An **obstruction** is the configuration defined in the source's preceding construction.

**Obstruction excluded-minor conjecture.** If $\Delta$ has an obstruction, then $M(\Delta)$ is an excluded minor for $\mathcal{BO}$.

The authors state this conjecture cautiously because Ingleton did not specify the construction of $M(\Delta)$ when $\Delta$ has an obstruction, and they cannot be certain that this is the matroid he intended. The assertion remains open.
330960.source_name: Joseph E. Bonin and Thomas J. Savitsky, “An infinite family of excluded minors for strong base-orderability”, arXiv:1507.05521 (2015).
330960.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05521

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

331192.title: The Motzkin product conjecture for entangled threads
331192.statement: Let an **even thread** be a thread of even type and an **odd thread** be a thread of odd type. For an even thread $\alpha$ and an odd thread $\beta$, consider the threads entangled with each of them. **Motzkin product conjecture.** For any even thread $\alpha$ and odd thread $\beta$, the number of odd threads entangled with $\alpha$, respectively the number of even threads entangled with $\beta$, is a product of Motzkin numbers. This conjecture predicts a uniform product formula extending the product formulas established for layered even and odd threads; proving it remains open.
331192.source_name: Eric S. Egge and Kailee Rubin, “Snow Leopard Permutations and Their Even and Odd Threads”, arXiv:1508.05310 (2016).
331192.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05310

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

331234.title: Aharoni and Berger's rainbow matching conjecture
331234.statement: Let $G$ be a multigraph whose edges are coloured with $n$ colours. Suppose that each colour class induces a matching of size $n+1$. **Aharoni and Berger's conjecture.** Then $G$ contains a rainbow matching of size $n$. The conjecture is a strengthening of rainbow matching results for properly edge-coloured bipartite multigraphs and is motivated by conjectures on transversals in Latin squares. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied source context.
331234.source_name: Dennis Clemens, Julia Ehrenmüller and Alexey Pokrovskiy, “On sets not belonging to algebras and rainbow matchings in graphs”, arXiv:1508.06437 (2015).
331234.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.06437

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).

331312.title: Qian's conjecture on extremal functions of disjoint graph minors
331312.statement:
Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be non-null graphs, and let $H$ be their disjoint union. The extremal function $c(H)$ is the supremum of $e(G)/v(G)$ over non-null graphs $G$ containing no $H$-minor.

**Qian's conjecture.** One should have

$$
c(H) \leq c(H_1)+c(H_2)+1.
$$

This would extend the proved bound for disjoint unions of $2$-connected graphs by removing the connectivity restriction on the components. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
331312.source_name: Endre Csóka, Irene Lo, Sergey Norin, Hehui Wu and Liana Yepremyan, “The extremal function for disconnected minors”, arXiv:1509.01185 (2015).
331312.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01185

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

331389.title: Erdős–Gyárfás monochromatic-same-color path cover conjecture
331389.statement:
Let $K_n$ be a complete graph whose edges are colored red and blue. A **same-color monochromatic path cover** is a collection of monochromatic paths, all in one common color, whose vertices cover $V(K_n)$.

**Erdős–Gyárfás same-color path cover conjecture.** The vertex set of every $2$-colored $K_n$ can be covered by at most

$$
\sqrt{n}
$$

monochromatic paths of the same color. This would be best possible.

A bound of $2\sqrt n$ is known. The sharper bound remains open.
331389.source_name: Andras Gyarfas, “Vertex covers by monochromatic pieces - A survey of results and problems”, arXiv:1509.05539 (2015).
331389.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05539

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2015). “Ryser's conjecture is open for $\alpha(G)=1$ except for $r\le 5$.”

331491.title: The matroidal Merino–Welsh conjectures
331491.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid without loops or coloops, and let $T(M;x,y)$ be its Tutte polynomial. **Matroidal Merino–Welsh conjectures.** The following inequalities hold:

$$
\max\left(T(M;2,0),T(M;0,2)\right)\geq T(M;1,1),
$$

$$
T(M;2,0)+T(M;0,2)\geq 2\cdot T(M;1,1),
$$

and

$$
T(M;2,0)\cdot T(M;0,2)\geq T(M;1,1)^2.
$$

These conjectures generalize the graphic inequalities through the Tutte-polynomial interpretations of spanning trees and orientations. The first inequality is known for paving matroids, Catalan matroids, and whirls, while the paper proves the multiplicative conjecture for lattice path matroids; the general matroidal conjectures remain open.
331491.source_name: Kolja Knauer, Leonardo Martínez-Sandoval and Jorge Luis Ramírez Alfonsín, “A Tutte polynomial inequality for lattice path matroids”, arXiv:1510.00600 (2016).
331491.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00600

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2015).

351310.title: Mohar's Kempe-equivalence conjecture for edge-colourings
351310.statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph. Two $k$-edge-colourings are **Kempe-equivalent** if one can be reached from the other through a series of Kempe changes using colours from $\{1,\ldots,k\}$. **Mohar's conjecture.** All $(\Delta(G)+2)$-edge-colourings of $G$ are Kempe-equivalent. This conjecture would strengthen Vizing's question, which asks whether every edge-colouring using more than the chromatic index can be reduced to an optimal colouring by Kempe changes. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.
351310.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Oscar Defrain, Tereza Klimošová, Aurélie Lagoutte and Jonathan Narboni, “On Vizing's edge colouring question”, arXiv:2107.07900 (2021).
351310.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2101.04065](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04065), [arXiv:1503.03430](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.03430).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07900

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

369970.title: Kelly's reconstruction conjecture for graphs
369970.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. For each vertex $v\in V(G)$, let $G_v$ be the subgraph obtained by deleting $v$ from $G$, and let

$$
D(G)=\{G_v\mid v\in V(G)\}
$$

be the multiset of all vertex-deleted subgraphs, called the **deck**. **Kelly's reconstruction conjecture.** Any two graphs $G$ and $H$ on $n>2$ vertices with equal multisets $D(G)$ and $D(H)$ are isomorphic. This is a classical open problem in graph theory: it asks whether a graph is determined up to isomorphism by its vertex-deleted subgraphs, although important special cases are known.
369970.source_name: David Hartman, Aneta Pokorná, Daniel Trlifaj and Lluís Vena, “Reconstructing graphs and their connectivity using graphlets”, arXiv:2508.19189 (2025).
369970.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1808.10034](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.10034), [arXiv:1406.7870](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.7870).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).
